book.title: Halloween Mazes for Kids
book.subtitle: 50 Mazes with a Spooky Story, Ages 6 to 10
book.author: Felicia Bauer

scenes.title: Where's The Costume Box?
scenes.text: Up in the attic, behind everything else. Jimmy has until dark.

scenes.title: The Stuck Zipper
scenes.text: The ghost suit is inside out and the zipper will not budge. Can you get Jimmy across to the sewing box?

scenes.title: Two White Swirls
scenes.text: Jimmy paints a white swirl on each cheek. Now he needs the tall mirror to find out if they came out spooky or silly.

scenes.title: Soup Before Sweets
scenes.text: Soup before sweets, says Mom.

scenes.title: Under The Couch Again
scenes.text: That is where the flashlight rolled. Pillows, boots, one lost sock. Help Jimmy dig it out.

scenes.title: High On The Closet Shelf
scenes.text: The pumpkin bucket is up where Jimmy can only just see it. Which way to the closet?

scenes.title: One Boot, Two Boot
scenes.text: One is waiting by the door. The other is hiding under the stairs, and Jimmy is hopping.

scenes.title: Out The Front Door
scenes.text: The porch light is on and the night smells like wet leaves. Only the coats between Jimmy and the door now.

scenes.title: Across The Stepping Stones
scenes.text: Wet leaves have covered every one of them. Can you find Jimmy a dry way to the little apple tree?

scenes.title: The Squeaky Gate
scenes.text: Squeeeak. That is the gate at the end of the yard, and the flower pots are in the way.

scenes.title: The First Porch
scenes.text: A grinning pumpkin sits by the steps. Jimmy practices saying trick or treat the whole way up.

scenes.title: Good Dog, Quiet Dog
scenes.text: The dog behind the fence is barking his head off and wagging his tail at the same time. Past him, quietly.

scenes.title: The Sprinkler Is On
scenes.text: A wet ghost is not a scary ghost. Time the dashes and keep Jimmy's sheet dry.

scenes.title: Taller Than Dad
scenes.text: That is how high these hedges are. Find the gaps and keep Jimmy going.

scenes.title: Sheets On The Line
scenes.text: White sheets flap on the line, and for a second Jimmy thinks they are other ghosts. The back gate is behind them.

scenes.title: The Corner Store
scenes.text: Orange lights fill the window. Jimmy wants the candy counter at the back, down one very narrow aisle.

scenes.title: Crunch
scenes.text: Somebody raked the whole street into one pile and Jimmy is going straight through it. Hold on to that bucket!

scenes.title: Pirates Everywhere
scenes.text: Pirates and robots and one very small dragon, all shouting at once. Can you get Jimmy through to the next porch?

scenes.title: The Spider Mailbox
scenes.text: A rubber spider swings from the mailbox. Jimmy knows it is rubber. Jimmy still ducks.

scenes.title: The Long Driveway
scenes.text: The last house on the street sits way back from the road. A long walk for one candy, but Jimmy is going anyway.

scenes.title: Into The Park
scenes.text: The gate is open, the sky has gone purple, and these trees looked a lot shorter this morning.

scenes.title: The Duck Pond
scenes.text: Ducks bob about under the first stars. Jimmy needs the stone bridge, and the mud in between is deep.

scenes.title: The Pumpkin Patch
scenes.text: Rows and rows of fat pumpkins, every one of them sitting in mud. Which way to the wagon?

scenes.title: Walls Made Of Hay
scenes.text: The bales are stacked higher than Jimmy's head, and somewhere in the middle of them a lantern is glowing.

scenes.title: Nobody On The Swings
scenes.text: They are moving anyway. Across the blacktop, somebody has left the gate open.

scenes.title: Kazoos And Bones
scenes.text: A skeleton band is playing on the bandstand, badly. Jimmy would like a much closer look.

scenes.title: The Bat Alley
scenes.text: Bats swoop over the alley lights, squeaking away. They are only saying hello to Jimmy. Probably.

scenes.title: The Fountain Square
scenes.text: Water splashes in the old stone fountain. Can you weave Jimmy past all these benches to the candy stand?

scenes.title: Drums!
scenes.text: The costume parade has filled the whole street, and Jimmy is on the wrong side of it.

scenes.title: The Treat Bowl Is Going
scenes.text: Paper bats swing over the library steps. Jimmy can see the bowl from here. Quick.

scenes.title: The Old Orchard
scenes.text: The apple trees lean right out over the grass, and Jimmy is looking for the stone wall on the far side.

scenes.title: The Cobweb Shed
scenes.text: Silver webs cover the shed door, every inch of it. There is a lantern in there, and Jimmy wants it.

scenes.title: Fog In The Lane
scenes.text: Thick as soup. Follow the fence posts with Jimmy and the streetlight will turn up eventually.

scenes.title: The Cat Will Not Move
scenes.text: A black cat has sat down in the middle of the lane, started purring, and will not move for anybody.

scenes.title: Along The Graveyard Fence
scenes.text: Old stones stand in rows behind the iron rails. Jimmy keeps close to the fence and does not look twice.

scenes.title: The Creaky Bridge
scenes.text: It creaks over a chuckling stream. Some of these boards are dry and some are not. Can you pick the dry ones?

scenes.title: The Whispering Willow
scenes.text: The willow trails its branches right across the path. They only feel like fingers.

scenes.title: Up To The Lighthouse
scenes.text: The beam swings over the rocks and back again. The keeper keeps a candy dish at the top of all those steps.

scenes.title: Tap, Tap, Clack
scenes.text: The skeletons are dancing in the old barn and the fiddler shows no sign of stopping. Jimmy taps one foot.

scenes.title: The Owl In The Loft
scenes.text: A very round owl blinks down at Jimmy. Jimmy blinks back, then goes looking for the open door.

scenes.title: The Mansion Gates
scenes.text: Tall iron gates at the top of the hill, and one of them is open. Jimmy just has to work out which.

scenes.title: A Maze Inside A Maze
scenes.text: There is a stone bench right at the middle of this one. Can you get Jimmy to it?

scenes.title: The Grand Porch
scenes.text: Cobwebs hang all the way across. Behind them somewhere is a brass bell the size of Jimmy's head.

scenes.title: The Great Hall
scenes.text: Candles flicker the whole length of it, and the ghost that waltzes past does not even look at Jimmy.

scenes.title: Down The Cellar Steps
scenes.text: Jars of pickles line the wall, hundreds of them. Jimmy needs the light switch, and it is past all these crates.

scenes.title: Up And Up And Up
scenes.text: The tower stairs curl around forever, and the bats do not mind sharing so long as Jimmy keeps left.

scenes.title: Still Playing
scenes.text: Nobody has been in this ballroom for years. Help Jimmy across to the tall glass doors.

scenes.title: The Mansion Attic
scenes.text: Trunks, old hats, and a smell like the back of a closet. Jimmy can see a round window at the far end.

scenes.title: The Last Big House
scenes.text: Paper ghosts, last porch of the night. Knock, trick or treat, bucket out, thank you. A whole night of practice, and Jimmy gets it exactly right.

scenes.title: Home At Last
scenes.text: Jimmy's own porch light is glowing warm and yellow. Get him to the steps, then tip out the bucket and count.

endPage.title: The End
endPage.text: Tip it all out on the floor and count. Jimmy's first Halloween was one to remember.

howToPlay: Find a path from Jimmy to the candy bucket. Wherever he is going, the bucket marks the finish.
You cannot walk through a wall.
Pick up as much candy as you can on the way.
Color in one box for every candy you get.
Write how many you got in the Total box.
See how close you came to the “Best possible” score.
Stuck? The answers are at the back.
The mazes get bigger as you go: 1 to 20 suit ages 6 and 7, 21 to 40 ages 8 and 9, and 41 to 50 ages 10 and up.

meetPage.title: Meet Jimmy
lines: It is Jimmy's very first Halloween, and he has never been trick-or-treating.
He does not quite know how it works yet, but he is going the long way round,
because the long way round is where the good candy is.
He needs somebody to find the path. That is you.
For everyone who takes the long way round. Happy Halloween.
